items.title: Family-written diaries are rarely studied on their own
items.whyItMatters: The unit's question is about diaries written by relatives, yet the review of controlled studies found only three that used them (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Separate family-written from staff-written and mixed diaries in every table of the review and say where the evidence is indirect.

items.title: Reading can harm patients with high symptoms
items.whyItMatters: Distress on first reading is usually brief, but intrusive memories cluster in patients with high symptoms beforehand (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Give the timing and support of reading its own section and draw practice points on screening before reading.

items.title: Unequal offer and uptake
items.whyItMatters: Families with a different language or without a regular visitor are much less likely to receive a diary (claim c4), which the local programme may repeat.
items.opportunity: Report programme delivery by who is offered a diary, and compare with the unit's own figure of 118 of 231 families.

items.title: Outcomes in bereaved relatives
items.whyItMatters: Before-after results in relatives change when bereaved relatives are excluded, so pooled statements may hide different effects.
items.opportunity: Report findings for bereaved relatives separately where studies allow.

items.title: Risk of an uncritical narrative review
items.whyItMatters: A narrative review can cite selectively and overstate a fragile pooled effect.
items.opportunity: Use a documented search, a charting form and a second checker, and state certainty for each conclusion.

errorsFound: The need's phrase 'treat diaries as proven' is not supported: the pooled effect in patients disappears when high-risk studies are removed.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a structured narrative review organised around effects, harms and delivery, with family-written diaries separated and certainty stated for each conclusion.
summary: Five gaps: indirect evidence on family-written diaries, reading harms, unequal uptake, bereaved relatives and the method risk of a narrative review.
